artiest/james-jamerson.text:
James Jamerson was born on 29 January 1936 on Edisto Island in South Carolina. He was raised partly by his grandmother, who played the piano, and he listened to gospel, blues and jazz on the radio. In 1954 he moved to Detroit with his mother. At high school he began playing the double bass, and before long he was working in the city's blues and jazz clubs.

From 1959 he was a permanent fixture at Hitsville U.S.A., the studio of Berry Gordy and Motown. He belonged to the core of session musicians who called themselves The Funk Brothers and who play on the vast majority of Motown records of the 1960s. In the early 1960s he switched from the double bass to an electric Fender Precision. His bass can be heard on My Girl by The Temptations, You Can't Hurry Love by The Supremes, Dancing in the Street by Martha and the Vandellas, Reach Out I'll Be There by The Four Tops and most of What's Going On by Marvin Gaye. He played on 23 number ones on the American pop chart.

Before Jamerson, a bass player mostly played root notes and simple patterns. He turned them into flowing, melodic lines, with chromatic runs and syncopation, that nevertheless stayed locked to the groove of the drums. Bass players from Paul McCartney to Sting and Flea name him as an influence. Even so, he was not credited on a sleeve until 1971. After Motown moved to Los Angeles he faded from view, and he died there on 2 August 1983 of the effects of alcoholism.
artiest/james-jamerson.listen: Listen to What's Going On by Marvin Gaye (1971) and focus on the bass alone. Notice how Jamerson never stands still: he plays free, singing lines full of little runs, yet stays exactly in the groove of the drums.

artiest/james-newton-howard.text: James Newton Howard was born in Los Angeles in 1951 and began piano lessons at the age of four. He studied at the Music Academy of the West. He then played keyboards in Elton John's band and wrote string arrangements for his songs. His first film score was Dune (1984), written with David Paich. Pretty Woman (1990), The Prince of Tides (1991) and The Fugitive (1993) followed. He made eight films with the director M. Night Shyamalan, including The Sixth Sense (1999). Together with Hans Zimmer he wrote the music for Batman Begins (2005) and The Dark Knight (2008). The Hunger Games films came later. He received nine Oscar nominations.
artiest/james-newton-howard.listen: Notice the difference between the lyrical piano melody of his early work and the tension Howard builds for Shyamalan with low strings and quiet, ominous chords.

artiest/james-p-johnson.text: James P. Johnson is called the father of stride piano. He grew up in New Jersey, learned classical music and ragtime, and played in clubs and at rent parties in New York. His Carolina Shout appeared as a piano roll in 1918 and on record in 1921; pianists learned the piece by heart, note for note. For Broadway he wrote the song Charleston (1923), which set off a dance craze. Johnson accompanied Bessie Smith and was Fats Waller's teacher. He also wanted to be recognised as a composer of concert music and wrote, among other things, the rhapsody Yamekraw. After a stroke in 1951 he could no longer play; he died in 1955.
artiest/james-p-johnson.listen: Notice how the left hand alternates between a low bass note and a chord, beneath a busy right hand.

artiest/james-reese-europe.text: James Reese Europe was the most important organiser of Black musicians in New York before the First World War. In 1910 he founded the Clef Club, a union and booking agency, and in 1912 he conducted a concert by a large Black orchestra at Carnegie Hall. With his Society Orchestra he accompanied the famous dance duo Vernon and Irene Castle. In 1913 he became one of the first Black bandleaders to make records. During the war he led the band of the 369th Infantry Regiment, the Harlem Hellfighters, who introduced ragtime and early jazz to audiences in France. Shortly after his return, in 1919, he was stabbed by one of his own musicians and died.
artiest/james-reese-europe.listen: Hear how a military brass band plays syncopation and blues: a step between ragtime and jazz.

artiest/james-taylor.text:
James Taylor is an American singer-songwriter and guitarist, born in Boston in 1948. He grew up in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, in a large musical family: his brothers and sister Alex, Livingston, Kate and Hugh also became musicians. His breakthrough came with Fire and Rain, in 1970. In 1971 he had his first number one with You've Got a Friend, written by Carole King.

Taylor is known for his gentle voice and his precise fingerpicking on the acoustic guitar. He wrote songs such as Sweet Baby James and recorded cover versions, such as How Sweet It Is (To Be Loved by You) and Handy Man. The compilation Greatest Hits from 1976 is one of the best-selling albums ever in the United States. Every album he released between 1977, beginning with JT, and 2007 sold more than a million copies. In the 1990s and 2000s his career revived with, among others, Hourglass, October Road and Covers. In 2015 he had his first number one album with Before This World. He also played the lead role in the film Two-Lane Blacktop (1971).

Taylor won six Grammys and entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2000. He is regarded as the most important voice of the singer-songwriter wave of the early 1970s, in which personal, restrained songs took centre stage. He continues to perform.
artiest/james-taylor.listen: Listen to Fire and Rain and notice how little there is to hear: an acoustic guitar and a quiet voice. Hear how the personal tone carries the song.

artiest/jamie-principle.text:
Jamie Principle is an American house musician, singer and producer, born in Chicago in 1960. He is one of the makers of the very first house, the dance music that emerged in the clubs of Chicago in the mid-1980s.

His 1984 track Your Love is regarded as one of the first house records. The lyrics came from a poem he wrote for his girlfriend at the time. Principle made music for it at home and recorded it on a four-track recorder. A friend gave a tape to the DJ Frankie Knuckles, who played the track again and again at the club The Power Plant. Fans recorded it there and passed on copies, so that the track was an underground club hit for more than a year before it was officially released on record. Knuckles's name also often appeared on his later records, such as Baby Wants to Ride. In 1992 Principle released the album The Midnite Hour, and he co-wrote I'm Not Over You by CeCe Peniston.

Principle shows how house came into being: not in a big studio, but at home, on a tape, and through the DJ and the crowd in the club. His soft, sensitive singing gave early house an emotional side. In 2004, with Back N Da Day, together with Knuckles, he topped the American dance chart. Later he sang on tracks by Gorillaz.
artiest/jamie-principle.listen: Listen to Your Love in the version by Frankie Knuckles (1987). Notice the arpeggio that runs through the whole track and Principle's vocals, which float over it almost like gospel.

artiest/jamiroquai.text:
Jamiroquai is an English band from London that plays acid jazz and funk. The group was formed in 1992 around the singer Jay Kay, the only constant through all the changes of line-up. The name is a blend of jam and a slightly altered version of the Iroquois, the Native American confederacy. Kay wanted a real live band with a real live sound, after he had had an earlier recording of When You Gonna Learn reworked by his producer. When it was restored to its original form, it became the debut single, a song about social issues.

Kay signed to Acid Jazz Records in 1991 after a demo on which he covered a song by the Brand New Heavies. Wallis Buchanan also played didgeridoo in the band, and the keyboard player Toby Smith was his writing partner. Later the band moved to Sony. Three albums reached number 1 in the United Kingdom: Emergency on Planet Earth (1993), Synkronized (1999) and A Funk Odyssey (2001), as did the single Deeper Underground (1998). Travelling Without Moving (1996) earned a Guinness World Record as the best-selling funk album ever. The video for Virtual Insanity won an MTV Video Music Award in 1997 and brought a Grammy in 1998.

The group built on acid jazz and later took in influences from rock, disco, electronic music and Latin. The lyrics addressed social and environmental issues. Jamiroquai was the third best-selling British act of the 1990s, after the Spice Girls and Oasis, and helped funk find a new audience.
artiest/jamiroquai.listen: Listen to When You Gonna Learn and notice the didgeridoo at the start and the warm funk groove with Jay Kay's vocals: how does the combination of the ancient instrument and the modern band sound?

artiest/jan-akkerman.text:
Jan Akkerman is a Dutch guitarist and lutenist, born in Amsterdam in 1946, the son of a dealer in rags and scrap metal. He began on the accordion and then switched to guitar. At thirteen he already played on a single, with the Friendship Sextet. With a scholarship he studied for five years at the Muzieklyceum in Amsterdam. He played in bands such as Johnny and his Cellar Rockers, The Hunters and Brainbox, and after a concert by the guitarist Julian Bream he became fascinated by Renaissance music and the lute.

At the end of 1969 he joined the trio of Thijs van Leer, which played the music for the Dutch version of the musical Hair. As Focus, the group made progressive rock, a mixture of classical, jazz and rock. Hocus Pocus and Sylvia became international hits, and the albums Focus II (1971) and Focus 3 (1972) sold well in America. In 1973 the readers of the British magazine Melody Maker voted him best guitarist, ahead of celebrities such as Jimmy Page. After Focus he continued as a solo artist. On Tabernakel (1973) he plays the lute, and Eli (1976) won an Edison.

Akkerman kept searching for new sounds, with jazz rock, guitar synthesizers and self-built tunings. He was one of the few Dutch musicians who challenged the British and American guitar heroes, and he played with artists from André Hazes to B.B. King. In 1992 he was seriously injured in a car accident, but a year later he was back on stage.
artiest/jan-akkerman.listen: Listen to Hocus Pocus by Focus. Notice Akkerman's fast, incisive guitar playing between the yodelling and Thijs van Leer's flute.

artiest/jan-garbarek.text: Jan Garbarek, from Norway, heard John Coltrane on the radio as a teenager and decided to become a saxophonist. In the 1960s he played with the American composer George Russell, who was then living in Scandinavia. From 1970 he recorded for ECM and became one of the label's best-known voices. His tone is clear, long-sustained and heavily reverberant, with influences from Norwegian folk music. He played in Keith Jarrett's European quartet. With the vocal ensemble The Hilliard Ensemble he made Officium (1994), on which he improvises over medieval church music; the album was a great commercial success.
artiest/jan-garbarek.listen: Hear the long, clear saxophone tone that hangs in the air.

artiest/jan-hammer.text: Jan Hammer was born in Prague in 1948 and studied at the music academy there. After the Warsaw Pact invasion in 1968 he left for the United States, where he received a scholarship to Berklee in Boston. From 1971 he played keyboards in guitarist John McLaughlin's Mahavishnu Orchestra. He was one of the first to play the Minimoog live. From 1984 he wrote the music for the police series Miami Vice, for roughly ninety episodes, in his own studio on a farm in New York State. The Miami Vice Theme was number one on the American chart in 1985 and won two Grammys. It was 2013 before another instrumental track topped the chart.
artiest/jan-hammer.listen: Notice how Hammer plays everything himself on synthesizers and electronic drums: a tight beat, fat bass lines and melodies that sometimes sound like an electric guitar.

artiest/jan-kincaid.text:
Jan Kincaid is a British drummer and one of the founders of The Brand New Heavies, an English band that started in 1985. Together with Simon Bartholomew and Andrew Levy he formed the group, which was then still called Brother International. The band recorded a demo that was played at the club The Cat in the Hat. Thanks to the good response, the group was booked there.

In 1989 the second single, People Get Ready, appeared. The group added the singer Jaye Ella Ruth and recorded the first album, which was released on 1 June 1990. On the record company's advice, the American singer N'Dea Davenport joined in 1990. With her vocals the album was reissued in 1991 on Delicious Vinyl. It reached number twenty-four on the British album chart. Singles such as Never Stop, Dream Come True and Don't Let It Go to Your Head were successful. After a singer left in 2000, the band's popularity declined, until Davenport returned in 2006 and the album Get Used to It was released. In 2009 the live album Live in London followed, and in 2013 the album Forward.

The Brand New Heavies are regarded as one of the most important bands of acid jazz, a style in which jazz, funk and soul meet dance music. They sold more than two and a half million records. As drummer, Kincaid held the rhythm of that music together, beneath the playing of the other musicians and Davenport's vocals.
artiest/jan-kincaid.listen: Listen to Never Stop and notice the drums: how does the rhythm keep the song tight, and how does the band leave room for the vocals?

artiest/jan-pieterszoon-sweelinck.text: Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck was organist of the Oude Kerk in Amsterdam for more than forty years, in the employ of the city. Because Calvinist worship had no organ playing, he played for the people of Amsterdam before and after the services, and students from Germany travelled specially to study with him. In his variations on the song Mein junges Leben hat ein End he embellishes a simple melody ever more richly. Through students such as Samuel Scheidt and Heinrich Scheidemann, a line runs on to Buxtehude and Bach.
artiest/jan-pieterszoon-sweelinck.listen: Listen to Mein junges Leben hat ein End and first hear the bare melody; then count how the ornaments around it grow busier and busier.

artiest/jan-pijnenburg.text:
Jan Pijnenburg is a Dutch drummer, born in Vught in 1955. After an unfinished course in graphic design, he trained as a pop music teacher at the conservatoire in Rotterdam. He played in numerous bands, including Lucifer, where he succeeded Henny Huisman, Hollander and Long Tall Ernie and the Shakers. Just before joining Doe Maar he was still touring Germany with a rock band.

In 1982 he succeeded René van Collem as drummer of Doe Maar, the band that mixed punk, ska and reggae with Dutch lyrics and became enormously popular in those years. Pijnenburg had played only one concert with the group when, in April 1982, on the way to the second gig, he was in a serious car accident. He needed more than half a year to recover, and Van Collem temporarily took his place again. On the album 4us (1983) a drum machine can therefore be heard on a number of tracks, such as Nachtzuster, Pa and Heroïne. On the live album Lijf aan lijf (1983) Pijnenburg does play himself.

After Doe Maar broke up in 1984 he drummed in, among others, The Magnificent 7, with Henny Vrienten, and in a new version of Shocking Blue. At the Doe Maar reunion in 2000 he played on the album Klaar and at the concerts in Ahoy, the Rotterdam arena, and in 2008 at the shows in De Kuip, the Rotterdam football stadium. Later he settled in Spain, where he has a studio.
artiest/jan-pijnenburg.listen: Listen to Pa by Doe Maar, from the album 4us (1983). Notice the tight, mechanical beat of the drum machine and compare it with the loose, living drumming on a live recording by the band.

artiest/jan-smit.text:
Jan Smit is a Dutch singer, television presenter and actor, born on 31 December 1985. He mostly sings Dutch-language songs in the genre known as palingsound (the Volendam sound, named after the town's eel-fishing tradition). His musical career began in Volendam, where he sang in the boys' choir De Zangertjes van Volendam. At the age of ten he was discovered by the band BZN, who asked him for a duet with the singer Carola Smit. The song Mama was a great success. After that he got a solo song, produced by three members of BZN: Ik Zing Dit Lied Voor Jou Alleen. It became the first song ever to enter the Dutch Top 40 at number one.

He was successful in the Netherlands and also in Belgium, Germany, Austria, Italy and France. For a time he performed mainly in Germany, where the rules for underage performers were less strict. Until 2005 he was called Jantje Smit. Then he changed his name, and on 25 March the reality series Gewoon Jan Smit began, which won the Gouden Televizier-Ring that year. In 2006 he received an Edison as best national singer for the album Jansmit.com and, with Als de Morgen is Gekomen and Cupido, scored his third and fourth number ones.

Later he became a TV presenter, including on Beste Zangers. In 2015 he joined the schlager trio Klubbb3 and in 2017 the Toppers. Smit showed how a child star from Volendam could build a broad, lasting career in television and Dutch-language music.
artiest/jan-smit.listen: Listen to Ik Zing Dit Lied Voor Jou Alleen and notice the voice of the young singer: how does his tone sound, and what do the strings and the melody around him do?

artiest/jane-s-addiction.text:
Jane's Addiction was an American rock band, formed in Los Angeles in 1985. The best-known line-up consisted of singer Perry Farrell, bassist Eric Avery, drummer Stephen Perkins and guitarist Dave Navarro. Farrell and Avery founded the group when Farrell's previous band Psi Com fell apart. They bonded over their love of Joy Division. The name refers to Jane Bainter, a housemate of Farrell's who was their muse, and also plays on the word chains. First came a drummer who never turned up to rehearsals. Then came Perkins, and through him Navarro as well.

The band became a sensation in the clubs of Los Angeles. The first album, the live album Jane's Addiction from 1987, attracted the attention of Warner Bros. The two studio albums Nothing's Shocking from 1988 and Ritual de lo Habitual from 1990 were well received and gave the band a growing audience. Jane's Addiction was one of the first bands from the alternative rock movement of the early 1990s to achieve commercial success.

In 1997 the band briefly returned, with Flea of the Red Hot Chili Peppers on bass. A second reunion followed in 2001, and in 2003 the third studio album, Strays, appeared. In 2008 the original line-up came together again. In 2022 Avery returned, and Navarro was temporarily replaced. A 2024 tour was cut short after Farrell pushed and hit Navarro on stage. The band proved that alternative rock could move from the club to a large audience.
artiest/jane-s-addiction.listen: Listen to a track from Ritual de lo Habitual and notice the bass and the drums: how do they build a groove, and how does Farrell use his voice on top?

artiest/janet-baker.text:
Dame Janet Baker is an English mezzo-soprano, best known as an opera, concert and lieder singer. She was born on 21 August 1933 in Hatfield in Yorkshire. Her father was an engineer and choir singer. She first worked at a bank and in 1953 moved to London, where she studied with Meriel St Clair and Helene Isepp. Isepp's son Martin became her regular accompanist. In 1956 she was knocked down by a bus and suffered concussion and lasting back pain. The same year she came second in the Kathleen Ferrier Memorial competition and made her stage debut, at the Oxford University Opera Club, and at Glyndebourne.

In 1959 she sang Eduige in Handel's Rodelinda, later among others Ariodante, of which she made a well-known recording with Raymond Leppard. With the English Opera Group in Aldeburgh she sang Purcell's Dido and Aeneas in 1962 and in works by Benjamin Britten, such as The Rape of Lucretia. At Glyndebourne she sang Dido again in 1966 and roles in Cavalli's La Calisto and Monteverdi's Il ritorno d'Ulisse. Her career lasted from the 1950s to the 1980s.

Baker is especially close to Baroque music, early Italian opera and the work of Britten. She was considered an exceptional singer and actress, admired for her dramatic intensity, which was best heard in her interpretation of Dido, the tragic queen. She showed that singing can be more than a beautiful voice, because every note carries a feeling.
artiest/janet-baker.listen: Listen to her Dido in the closing lament When I am laid in earth and notice the descending line in the bass: how does her voice follow the despair, and where does she hold back?

artiest/janet-jackson.text:
Janet Jackson was born in 1966 in Gary, Indiana, the youngest of the ten children of the Jackson family. She began as an actress in television series such as Good Times and Fame. Her first album appeared in 1982 and got no further than number 63 on the Billboard 200. Only four years later did she find her own sound.

For Control (1986) she worked with Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis, two producers from Minneapolis from the circle around Prince. They recorded in their studio Flyte Tyme. The sound was tight and electronic, with drum machines and synthesizers. Control reached number 1 on the Billboard 200. When I Think of You became her first number 1 on the Hot 100. She and her brother Michael thereby became the only brother and sister who both had a solo number 1 on that chart. On Rhythm Nation 1814 (1989) she continued with the same producers. That album yielded seven singles that reached the top 5 of the Hot 100, the only album ever to do so.

janet. (1993) and The Velvet Rope (1997) also entered at number 1. In 1993 she starred opposite 2Pac in the film Poetic Justice. After the uproar over her Super Bowl halftime performance in 2004, part of radio and TV shunned her music, which damaged the sales of later albums. In 2019 she was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. In her speech she asked the organisation to induct more women.
artiest/janet-jackson.listen: When I Think of You showcases the Minneapolis sound of Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis. Notice the tight drum machine pattern and the short, sharp synthesizer chords that fall between the vocal lines.

artiest/janine-jansen.text:
Janine Jansen is a Dutch violinist and violist. She was born on 7 January 1978 in Soest, into a musical family. Her father Jan plays organ, harpsichord and piano and was organist of St Martin's Cathedral in Utrecht from 1987 to 2011. Her mother was a classical singer and her brother David is a harpsichordist and cellist. In 1991 and 1993 she took part in the Menuhin Competition for juniors, and in 1991 she reached the final. She is married to the Swedish conductor Daniel Blendulf and lives in Utrecht.

In 2001 she played Brahms's Violin Concerto as a soloist with the National Youth Orchestra of Scotland. In 2005 she opened the BBC Proms. She chose her own path by recording with only five solo strings instead of an orchestra, with her brother as cellist and her father as continuo player. At live concerts she received standing ovations, for example at the concert with the Berliner Philharmoniker in 2006 in the Waldbühne in Berlin. She played famous violins, such as the 1727 Stradivarius Barrere and the 1727 Baron Deurbroucq, and later the Rivaz, Baron Gutmann of 1707.

She began her own chamber music festival in Utrecht and has been a member of Spectrum Concerts Berlin since 1998. In 2003 she won the Dutch Music Prize, and in 2009 the Instrumentalist Award of the Royal Philharmonic Society in Great Britain. Jansen showed that a Dutch violinist could conquer the international concert stages, and brought classical music to a large audience with a personal, intimate style of playing.
artiest/janine-jansen.listen: Listen to her recording of Brahms's Violin Concerto and notice the opening of the violin: how long does she sustain the tone, and how does she adapt the colour when the orchestra enters?

artiest/janis-joplin.text:
Janis Joplin was an American singer, born in 1943 in Port Arthur, Texas. At high school she felt like an outsider. Through friends she heard records by blues singers such as Bessie Smith and Ma Rainey, and that gave her the idea of singing herself. She sang blues and folk in Austin and in 1963 hitchhiked to San Francisco. There she got involved with drugs, after which she returned to Texas to get clean.

In 1966 the promoter Chet Helms brought her back to San Francisco, as singer of the psychedelic rock band Big Brother and the Holding Company. The breakthrough came in June 1967 with their performance at the Monterey Pop Festival. The album Cheap Thrills (1968), with Piece of My Heart, Summertime and a live version of Ball and Chain, made her a star. She then went solo, with the Kozmic Blues Band and later the Full Tilt Boogie Band, and in 1969 she appeared at Woodstock. In October 1970 she died at the age of 27 from a heroin overdose. Three months later Pearl appeared, with Me and Bobby McGee and the a cappella Mercedes Benz, her last recording.

Joplin had a powerful, raw voice that screamed, cracked and pleaded. She brought the blues of her role models to the rock of the hippie era and showed that a woman could play the lead role there. In 1995 she was inducted as the first female solo artist into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in the first year that this was possible.
artiest/janis-joplin.listen: Listen to Piece of My Heart (1968) by Big Brother and the Holding Company. Notice how Joplin lets her voice break and scream in the chorus, while the guitars sound raw and rough.

artiest/janos-bihari.text:
János Bihari was a Hungarian violinist from a Romani family. He was born on 21 October 1764 in Nagyabony, now Veľké Blahovo in Slovakia, and died on 26 April 1827 in Pest. His father was also a violinist. In 1801 Bihari put together an orchestra in Pest with one cimbalom player and four violinists. That orchestra quickly became popular and travelled with him to many cities in Hungary and abroad. He also played at parties and banquets and performed during the Congress of Vienna in 1814.

Bihari is regarded as one of the founders of academic Romani music and of the genre verbunkos, a Hungarian style that was originally played at military recruitment. In the mid-nineteenth century so-called Gypsy music was a craze, and Bihari was the first great name. Franz Liszt described his violin tones as tears flowing down the enchanted ears. Melodies by Bihari were used by composers such as Liszt, Beethoven and Pablo de Sarasate.

In 1824 he lost the use of his left hand for playing, after injuring it. After that his popularity declined and he died in poverty. He left eighty-four compositions, which are regarded as classics. His music shows how a folk musician from Hungary could influence the classical world, and how the fast, fiery style of the verbunkos later found its way into the concert hall.
artiest/janos-bihari.listen: Listen to a verbunkos, for example in an arrangement for violin and cimbalom, and notice the rhythm: where does a slow, proud section alternate with a fast and fiery one?

artiest/japan.text:
Japan was an English new wave band, formed in 1974 in Catford in south London. The brothers David Sylvian, vocals and guitar, and Steve Jansen, drums, met bassist Mick Karn at the same school, Catford Boys. At first they played two chords and used the music mainly to escape their surroundings. The following year schoolfriend Richard Barbieri joined on keyboards, and later the guitarist Rob Dean. The name Japan was meant to be temporary, but it stuck. After signing the record contract, Sylvian, Jansen and Karn adopted stage names.

In March 1978 the first single appeared, a version of Don't Rain on My Parade, and a month later the debut album Adolescent Sex. The campaign around their androgynous glam rock image attracted little interest in England, but it did catch on in Japan. The first albums were out of step in a time of punk and new wave and did not reach the charts. Influences were Lou Reed, T. Rex, New York Dolls, Roxy Music and David Bowie. In 1979 the band came to the country of Japan for the first time and filled the Budokan, with eleven thousand seats, three days in a row.

Later the group developed its own sound and found success in England, with nine hits in the top forty, including the single Ghosts in 1982. The live album Oil on Canvas reached the British top five in 1983. Six albums went gold. The band broke up in December 1982, just as it was also becoming successful in other countries. Japan showed that a band with electronic sounds and cool vocals could go on to influence a great deal of British pop music.
artiest/japan.listen: Listen to Ghosts and notice the space in the track: which sounds are there, how little does the rhythm move, and how does the voice sound against that?

artiest/jascha-heifetz.text:
Jascha Heifetz was a Russian-American violinist, seen by many as one of the greatest violinists of all time. He was born on 2 February 1901 in Vilna, now Vilnius, into a Jewish family. His father Reuven was a violinist, violin teacher and concertmaster of the orchestra of the Vilna Theatre. In 1906 Jascha, five years old, went to music school, with Ilya Malkin. He was regarded as a child prodigy and made his debut at seven in Kovno with Mendelssohn's Violin Concerto. In 1910 he entered the class of the Russian violin school in Saint Petersburg. In 1912 he met Fritz Kreisler in Berlin.

As a teenager he played in a large part of Europe. In April 1911 he gave an open-air concert in Saint Petersburg for twenty-five thousand people, so excited that police had to protect him. In 1914 he played with the Berliner Philharmoniker. To escape the Russian Revolution his family left Russia in 1917, via the Far East and by ship to San Francisco. On 27 October 1917 he played at Carnegie Hall for the first time, and it was an instant sensation. At eighteen he was the highest-paid violinist in the world.

He had a long concert career and played for the USO during the war. After an injury to his right arm in 1972, the bowing arm, he turned to teaching. He died in 1987. Heifetz showed how pure and technically controlled a violin can sound, and his recordings remained a benchmark for later violinists. Itzhak Perlman later recounted that a Heifetz recital on the radio had led him to the violin.
artiest/jascha-heifetz.listen: Listen to his recording of Mendelssohn's Violin Concerto and notice the purity and the speed in the last movement: how steady does the tone stay, even as the notes fly past?

artiest/jason-donovan.text:
Jason Donovan was born on 1 June 1968 in Malvern, a suburb of Melbourne. Both his parents were actors, and after their divorce his father raised him alone. At eleven he stood in front of the camera for the first time. In 1986 he was cast as Scott Robinson in the Australian soap Neighbours. The wedding of his character to Charlene, played by Kylie Minogue, made the series popular in England too.

Like Minogue, he chose pop music and signed to PWL, the label of Stock Aitken Waterman. The trio at first hesitated to take on a second soap star, but soon recorded his first single, Nothing Can Divide Us (1988), a song that Rick Astley had turned down. Then came the duet with Minogue, Especially for You, which reached number 1 in January 1989 and became the trio's biggest British hit. In March 1989 he had his first solo number 1 with Too Many Broken Hearts. His debut album Ten Good Reasons became the best-selling album of 1989 in England, and for a time he was at the top of both the album and the singles chart, with Sealed with a Kiss.

Donovan is a textbook example of the Stock Aitken Waterman method: a familiar face from television sings a song that is already largely finished in the studio. The second album, Between the Lines (1990), sold far fewer copies, and his popularity as a pop star declined. In the early 1990s he found a new role in the musical Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat.
artiest/jason-donovan.listen: Listen to Too Many Broken Hearts (1989). Notice the typical Stock Aitken Waterman production: a tight drum machine, glossy synthesizers and a melody that sticks at once, with Donovan's voice front and centre.

artiest/jason-marsalis.text:
Jason Marsalis is an American jazz drummer, vibraphonist, composer, producer and bandleader, a member of the musical Marsalis family. He was born on 4 March 1977 in New Orleans, the youngest son of Dolores Ferdinand Marsalis and the pianist and music teacher Ellis Marsalis. His brothers are Branford, Wynton, Delfeayo, Ellis III and Mboya Kenyatta, and the first three are also jazz musicians. He studied at the New Orleans Center for Creative Arts and at McMain Magnet Secondary School. In 1998, after three years, he left Loyola University, where he was studying classical music, to become a musician.

At six he took lessons from the New Orleans drummer James Black. As a teenager he made his recording debut on Delfeayo's Pontius Pilate's Decision in 1992. He worked as an accompanist in mainstream jazz, funk and jazz fusion, including with Neslort and Snarky Puppy, with the Brazilian percussion ensemble Casa Samba and in Celtic music with Beth Patterson. He put the percussionist Bill Summers in touch with the trumpeter Irvin Mayfield, which gave rise to Los Hombres Calientes. In 1994, at seventeen, he toured with the Marcus Roberts Trio with Gershwin for Lovers, and he continues to work with Roberts.

During the coronavirus years, with venues closed, he re-enrolled at Loyola and earned his degree in May 2026, thirty-one years after his first enrolment. Marsalis shows that the New Orleans jazz tradition is broad and encompasses more than trumpet and saxophone: his instruments are drums and vibraphone, and he also writes his own music.
artiest/jason-marsalis.listen: Listen to a recording with Marcus Roberts and notice the drums: how does Marsalis follow the pianist, and how does he place accents without drowning out the trio?

artiest/jason-quenneville.text:
Jason Quenneville is a Canadian producer and songwriter who works under the name DaHeala. He was born in 1982 and grew up in Gatineau, in Quebec, in a family where French and English were spoken. At thirteen he learned to DJ at a youth centre, and that is how he came to the music program FruityLoops, with which he began making beats. He did his first production work at twenty-three, for a mixtape by the rapper Belly.

From 2013 Quenneville worked closely with The Weeknd. He co-produced all the tracks on his album Kiss Land (2013) and was executive producer of Beauty Behind the Madness (2015). On that album he wrote and produced, among others, Earned It, which featured in the film Fifty Shades of Grey and was nominated for an Oscar. For Starboy (2016) he co-wrote five tracks, including the title track with Daft Punk. On After Hours (2020) he worked on the single Blinding Lights. He also worked for artists such as Halsey and Lil Uzi Vert.

Quenneville is an example of the people behind the scenes of the modern pop hit. His name is not printed large on the sleeve, but he writes and builds the songs together with the star and other producers, such as Max Martin. That is how a hit is often made today, in a team in which everyone contributes part of the song or the sound.
artiest/jason-quenneville.listen: Listen to Blinding Lights (2019) by The Weeknd. Notice the synthesizers and the fast, straight beat that recall the pop music of the 1980s.

artiest/jason-swinscoe.text:
Jason Swinscoe is a British musician, DJ and producer, born in 1972. He started playing the guitar at the age of six, but never received formal musical training. Instead he studied fine art at the art college in Cardiff, where in 1990 he founded the band Crabladder. In 1994 he became a DJ on a pirate radio station in south London.

Swinscoe then went to work at the London label Ninja Tune. There he fell under the spell of electronic music, abstract hip hop, nu jazz, drum and bass and ambient. In 1999 he founded The Cinematic Orchestra, the group that made him known. The first album Motion appeared that year, followed by Every Day (2002) and Ma Fleur (2007). Ma Fleur contains To Build a Home, with the singer Patrick Watson. The group also made new music for the silent film Man with a Movie Camera by Dziga Vertov.

The name of the group already says a lot: the music sounds like a soundtrack to a film you have to imagine yourself. Swinscoe works like a director, combining samples and electronics with real jazz musicians on double bass, drums, piano and brass. In doing so he was one of the makers who gave jazz a new audience in the late 1990s, through the clubs and DJ culture rather than the jazz club. Swinscoe also lived for a few years in Los Angeles, New York and Paris.
artiest/jason-swinscoe.listen: Listen to To Build a Home (2007) by The Cinematic Orchestra. Notice how the track begins with just piano and voice, and how strings slowly join in, making it ever fuller.

artiest/javier-navarrete.text:
Javier Navarrete is a Spanish composer, chiefly of film music. He was born in 1956 in Teruel and moved to Barcelona at nineteen. In 2012 he moved to Los Angeles. He wrote music for Spanish films such as Tras el cristal and Dot the I.

He became known internationally through his work with the director Guillermo del Toro. He composed the music for El espinazo del diablo from 2001 and for El laberinto del fauno from 2006, which is called Pan's Labyrinth in English. For the latter film he received an Academy Award nomination in 2007, alongside a Grammy nomination for the soundtrack and an Ariel Award. Mirrors, Inkheart, Cracks, Byzantium and Wrath of the Titans followed, among others. For the HBO film Hemingway & Gellhorn he won an Emmy in 2012. In 2015 he also wrote the music for the Hong Kong film Zhong Kui: Snow Girl and the Dark Crystal.

Navarrete writes orchestral music in which melody and atmosphere carry the images. His themes for Pan's Labyrinth suit the dark fairy-tale world of the film. The track Long, Long Time Ago from 2006 comes from that score. It shows that a film composer can evoke an entire story with one simple, recognisable theme. His work is an example of modern European film music and of the Spanish contribution to international cinema.
artiest/javier-navarrete.listen: Listen to Long, Long Time Ago and notice the simplicity of the melody: how gentle and fairy-tale-like does it sound, and what atmosphere does the track evoke before you even know the film?

artiest/javier-perianes.text:
Javier Perianes is a Spanish classical pianist, born on 24 September 1978 in Nerva. He plays at well-known festivals in Spain, such as Santander, Granada, Peralada and San Sebastián, and in concert series around the world, including at Carnegie Hall in New York. He often won prizes at competitions, including first prize and the gold medal at the forty-second Premio Jaén de Piano and first prize at the eighth piano competition of the Fundación Jacinto e Inocencio Guerrero. He was also a prizewinner at the Vianna da Motta in Lisbon.

He has worked with leading conductors such as Lorin Maazel, Daniel Barenboim, Zubin Mehta, Rafael Frühbeck de Burgos, Jesús López Cobos, Antoni Wit, Daniel Harding and Vasily Petrenko. His recordings for Harmonia Mundi were praised, including Schubert's Impromptus and Klavierstücke, sonatas by Manuel Blasco de Nebra and Música callada by Federico Mompou. In September 2011 an album of piano music by Manuel de Falla appeared on the same label. In 2015 he recorded Grieg's Piano Concerto, with the BBC Symphony Orchestra under Sakari Oramo, with a selection from Grieg's Lyric Pieces.

A reviewer for the Sunday Telegraph called him a natural Schubert player who let his playing sound beautiful. Perianes brings together Spanish and international piano music, from Mompou and De Falla to Schubert, Brahms and Debussy, and in doing so showed that the Spanish piano tradition has a broad place in concert life. His later albums include Scarlatti and work from Goyescas.
artiest/javier-perianes.listen: Listen to Schubert's Impromptus in his recording and notice the singing melody in the right hand: how softly does he play, and where does he let the tone ring out for a moment?

artiest/jay-kay.text:
Jay Kay is an English singer and songwriter, co-founder and singer of the acid jazz and funk band Jamiroquai. He was born Jason Luís Cheetham on 30 December 1969 in Stretford, Lancashire, the son of an English cabaret singer, Karen Kay, and a Portuguese guitarist, Luís Saraiva. His parents split up and he only got to know his biological father around the age of twenty-eight. His identical twin brother David died a few weeks after birth from brain damage.

In 1992 he founded Jamiroquai. The first members included Toby Smith on keyboards, Nick Van Gelder on drums, Stuart Zender on bass and Wallis Buchanan on didgeridoo. Derrick McKenzie has played drums since 1994. After the success of the first single When You Gonna Learn, Kay signed a million-pound contract with Sony. The band has sold more than twenty-six million albums. In 2017 he received the BMI President's Award at the BMI London Awards, and that same year he was seriously injured in his back, as a result of which two concerts in Tokyo were postponed.

Kay is also known for his distinctive hats and caps, which earned him the names the mad hatter and the cat in the hat. He has a fondness for expensive cars and appeared on Top Gear and Fifth Gear, and supported environmental causes. He combines funk and soul with a warm, sliding vocal style and a striking show, and in this way brought acid jazz to a large audience, far beyond the London clubs.
artiest/jay-kay.listen: Listen to When You Gonna Learn and notice the didgeridoo in the intro and the vocals: how does Kay use his voice, and which instruments make up the groove?

artiest/jay-mcshann.text:
Jay McShann, in full James Columbus McShann, was an American jazz pianist, singer, composer and bandleader. He was born on 12 January 1916 in Muskogee, Oklahoma, and was nicknamed Hootie. As a boy he taught himself to play the piano, by watching his sister's lessons and by playing melodies he heard on the radio. He was strongly influenced by the late-night broadcasts of the pianist Earl Hines from the Grand Terrace Cafe in Chicago. Of that time he said: when Fatha Hines went off the radio, I went to bed.

In 1936 he moved to Kansas City, Missouri, and formed his own big band there. Those who played in it included Charlie Parker from 1937 to 1942, Al Hibbler, Ben Webster, Paul Quinichette, Bernard Anderson, Gene Ramey and Jimmy Witherspoon. His first recordings were all with Parker. The band played swing and blues, but most of the records were blues. The best-known recording was Confessin' the Blues, with vocals by Walter Brown. In 1944 McShann was drafted into the army and the band broke up. When he came back two years later, small groups had taken the place of the big bands.

After the war he led small groups with the blues shouter Jimmy Witherspoon, who recorded with him from 1945 and had a hit in 1949 with Ain't Nobody's Business. In 2003 McShann said that players from Kansas City were recognised everywhere, on the coast and in the north and south. He showed what the Kansas City style was, a mixture of swing and blues, and that Charlie Parker took his first steps in such a band. He died on 7 December 2006.
artiest/jay-mcshann.listen: Listen to Confessin' the Blues and notice the interplay between singer and horns: how does the rhythm section keep the swing going, and what does the piano do in the gaps?

artiest/jay-z.text:
Jay-Z is an American rapper, entrepreneur and label boss. He was born Shawn Carter in Brooklyn in 1969 and grew up in the Marcy Houses, a public housing project. His father left the family when he was eleven. In the neighbourhood he was called Jazzy, and his stage name is a tribute to his mentor, the rapper Jaz-O. In the late 1980s he was already rapping on records by Jaz-O and later Big Daddy Kane.

Because no major label wanted him, Jay-Z sold his CDs from the boot of his car. With Damon Dash and Kareem Burke he founded Roc-A-Fella Records. The debut Reasonable Doubt (1996) was well received, and Vol. 2... Hard Knock Life (1998) became his biggest commercial success. The Blueprint (2001), with productions by, among others, Kanye West, gave his music a warmer sound with soul samples. The Black Album (2003), with 99 Problems, American Gangster (2007) and 4:44 (2017) followed. As a guest he rapped on hits such as Crazy in Love by Beyoncé and Umbrella by Rihanna, and with Alicia Keys he made Empire State of Mind.

Jay-Z is known for his intricate lyrics full of wordplay and double meanings, often about his journey from the street to the top. He was also a businessman: from 2004 to 2007 he ran Def Jam, where he helped Kanye West and Rihanna further, and later he started Roc Nation. In this way he became one of the most powerful figures behind the scenes of hip hop and pop.
artiest/jay-z.listen: Listen to Umbrella (2007) by Rihanna. Notice Jay-Z's short rap verse at the beginning, which opens the track before Rihanna starts singing.

artiest/jazz-epistles.text:
The Jazz Epistles were the first important bebop band in South Africa, even though the group existed only briefly. They drew inspiration from Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers. The members included Dollar Brand, later Abdullah Ibrahim, on piano, Kippie Moeketsi on alto saxophone, Jonas Gwangwa on trombone, Hugh Masekela on trumpet, Johnny Gertze on bass and Early Mabuza or Makaya Ntshoko on drums. The group became known through the jam sessions Jazz at the Odin at the Odin Theatre in Sophiatown.

The band was formed in the mid-1950s, when Brand and Mackay Davashe began working with Gwangwa and Masekela. In 1959, just before breaking up, they recorded the first album by a Black South African band, Jazz Epistle, Verse 1. That same year the musical King Kong by Todd Matshikiza became a hit in Johannesburg. With a jazz score, it told the tragic story of the boxer Ezekiel Dhlamini. Miriam Makeba, members of the Manhattan Brothers and the musicians of the Jazz Epistles worked on it.

After the Sharpeville massacre in 1960, apartheid became even harsher. Performances were banned and jazz was not allowed on the radio. When the makers of King Kong were invited to Europe, the government issued passports, expecting it to be propaganda. Many musicians chose exile in Europe. As a result, much of the most adventurous South African music developed outside the country for decades. In 2016 several members played two reunion concerts in Johannesburg after 56 years.
artiest/jazz-epistles.listen: Listen to Scullery Department and notice the alternation of trumpet and saxophone in the melody and the fast accompaniment: can you hear how bebop from America is played here with a South African feel?

artiest/jazzanova.text:
Jazzanova is a German DJ and producer collective from Berlin. The group was founded in 1995 by Alexander Barck, Claas Brieler, Jürgen von Knoblauch, Roskow Kretschmann, Stefan Leisering and Axel Reinemer. The DJs are Von Knoblauch, Barck and Brieler, and the producer trio consists of Reinemer, Leisering and Kretschmann. Their music is characterised by nu jazz, chill-out and Latin jazz, with influences from electro, house and soul. In 1997 they founded the record label Sonar Kollektiv.

The collective became known as remixers, for among others Incognito, 4Hero, MJ Cole, Ian Pooley and Masters at Work. It also has a side project, Extended Spirit. The second studio album, Of All the Things, appeared in October 2008. In May 2012 Funkhaus Studio Sessions followed, with Paul Randolph as singer, and in 2018 the group announced the album The Pool. They collaborated a great deal with other musicians.

Jazzanova showed that DJs and producers could build a musical world of their own with jazz, soul and dance music. The group used the freedom of the club to combine pieces of jazz records with electronic beats, and its own label gave room to other artists from that scene. In Germany the collective became a name within nu jazz, and its remix work also brought the music to the audience of British acid jazz, of which Incognito is an important name.
artiest/jazzanova.listen: Listen to a Jazzanova remix and notice the beat beneath the jazz melody: which sounds come from an old record, and which are electronic?

artiest/jean-baptiste-lully.text: Jean-Baptiste Lully came to Paris as an Italian teenager and became the most powerful musician at the court of Louis XIV. With the exclusive right to opera, he created, together with the poet Philippe Quinault, the tragédie en musique, a French form with a great deal of dance and a tightly drilled string ensemble. For Molière's Le bourgeois gentilhomme he wrote the Turkish ceremony. He died in 1687 from a wound caused by his own conducting staff, sustained during his Te Deum.
artiest/jean-baptiste-lully.listen: Listen to the Turkish march and hear how timpani and strings set up a solemn, almost military procession for a mock ceremony.

artiest/jean-benoit-dunckel.text:
Jean-Benoît Dunckel is a French musician, best known as one half of the French duo Air, together with Nicolas Godin. He was born on 7 September 1969. In the 1980s he formed the band Orange with Alex Gopher, Xavier Jamaux and Jean de Reydellet. He studied mathematics and physics and taught at a secondary school in Paris before becoming a professional musician. Since 1995 he has formed Air with his partner Godin.

Under the name Darkel he released his first solo album, titled Darkel, in September 2006. In 2011 he formed the electronic side project Tomorrow's World with Lou Hayter of New Young Pony Club, which released a first album in 2013. With the Icelander Barði Jóhannsson he worked under the name Starwalker, with an EP in 2014 featuring Losers Can Win and Bad Weather and an album in 2016. In 2015 the mini-album The Man of Sorrow appeared and he wrote the soundtrack for the film The Summer of Sangailé. In 2018 his second solo album, H+, followed.

In June 2022 he released the album Carbon on his own label Prototyp. On it he suggests that technology can save the world. Of the title he said that carbon does not disappear when you burn it and is full of power, because diamonds are crystallised carbon. In 2024 he wrote the film music for The Good Teacher. Dunckel combines electronic sounds and keyboards with a calm, floating atmosphere, and shows how a scientifically trained musician shapes synthesizers into a personal language.
artiest/jean-benoit-dunckel.listen: Listen to a track by Air on which Dunckel plays keyboards and notice the synthesizers: which sound carries the melody, and how calmly do the chords move beneath it?

artiest/jean-ferrat.text:
Jean Ferrat was a French chansonnier, composer and poet, born in 1930 as Jean Tenenbaum in Vaucresson, near Paris. His father, a Jewish jeweller of Russian origin, was arrested in 1942 and murdered in Auschwitz. The family went into hiding in the south of France and was helped there by communists. From then on Ferrat felt a bond with the French Communist Party, although he did not always agree with it.

In the early 1950s he began in the Parisian cabarets. In 1956 he set Les yeux d'Elsa, a poem by Louis Aragon, to music, and in 1960 he broke through with Ma môme. Nuit et brouillard (1963), about the deportations, and La montagne (1964), about life in the countryside of the Ardèche, where he went to live himself, followed. Ferrat adapted dozens of Aragon's poems into songs, such as Aimer à perdre la raison, and in 1971 Ferrat chante Aragon appeared. His song Ma France (1969) was for a time banned from French radio. In 1973 he stopped performing.

Ferrat was a committed singer, who showed that a chanson could be about anything, including war and injustice. His songs leaned on strong lyrics, with a warm voice and sober accompaniment by the orchestra of the arranger Alain Goraguer. He also had influence in the Netherlands: to the melody of La montagne, Friso Wiegersma wrote Het dorp, which made Wim Sonneveld famous. Ferrat died in 2010.
artiest/jean-ferrat.listen: Listen to La montagne (1964) and then to Het dorp by Wim Sonneveld. Notice how the same melody tells a story about a changing countryside in two languages.

artiest/jean-goldkette.text:
Jean Goldkette was a pianist and bandleader who left his mark on jazz in the 1920s mainly as an entrepreneur. His birthplace is not entirely certain: Valenciennes or Patras. He grew up in Greece and Russia, studied piano at the Moscow conservatoire and emigrated to the United States in 1911. In Detroit he rented a dance hall, formed an orchestra of his own and built up a business that booked about twenty orchestras and owned many dance halls. He himself mostly did not play.

His best-known group was the Victor Recording Orchestra, which made recordings from 1924 to 1929. The chief arranger was Bill Challis, and the line-up included, among others, Bix Beiderbecke, Hoagy Carmichael, Jimmy and Tommy Dorsey and the guitarist Eddie Lang. The orchestra sounded like a tightly rehearsed dance band with room for soloists. In a battle of the bands it is even said to have beaten the orchestra of Fletcher Henderson. Rex Stewart, who played with Henderson, called it the best dance band of its time.

In 1927 Goldkette lost his best players to Paul Whiteman, because he could no longer pay their salaries. In the 1930s he went bankrupt and worked as a booking agent and classical pianist. Even so, his influence remained great. He helped McKinney's Cotton Pickers and the orchestra of Glen Gray, later known as the Casa Loma Orchestra, get started. His bands formed a link between early jazz and the swing era of the big dance orchestras.
artiest/jean-goldkette.listen: Listen to a recording by the Victor orchestra from 1924 to 1929 and notice how the tight arrangements always leave room for a short solo by a horn player or the guitar.

artiest/jean-michel-jarre.text:
Jean-Michel Jarre is a French composer and electronic musician, born in 1948 in Lyon, the son of the film composer Maurice Jarre. In 1969 he went to work at the Groupe de Recherches Musicales in Paris, the studio of Pierre Schaeffer, the inventor of musique concrète. There he learned to work with sound as a material. With Oxygène (1976) he brought synthesizer music to an audience of millions.

Jarre recorded Oxygène between August and November 1976 in an improvised home studio in the kitchen of his Paris apartment. He used a handful of analogue instruments, including an ARP 2600, an EMS VCS 3, an Eminent organ, a Mellotron and a Korg Mini-Pops rhythm box. The album consists of six parts that flow into one another: floating blocks of chords, filtered noise that sounds like wind, and above it simple melodies. Oxygène was released in December 1976 on Disques Motors, reached number 1 in France and number 2 in England, where Oxygène (Part IV) reached number 4 as a single. The album is estimated to have sold some 18 million copies. Its successor Équinoxe followed in 1978.

Jarre then became known for his open-air concerts. On 14 July 1979 more than a million people came to the Place de la Concorde in Paris, and in 1986 even more came in Houston. In 1981 he gave five concerts in Beijing and Shanghai, as the first Western musician invited to China after Mao. Jarre showed that one person with a few synthesizers could make an entire album. In doing so he stands between the studio experiments of Schaeffer and the ambient and new age of the 1980s.
artiest/jean-michel-jarre.listen: In Oxygène, Pt. 4, listen to the rhythm section: it comes from a cheap Korg rhythm box with preset patterns. Above it Jarre plays a simple synthesizer melody, and in between, bursts of noise sweep like gusts of wind through the stereo image.

artiest/jean-paul-bluey-maunick.text:
Jean-Paul Maunick, almost always called Bluey, is a British guitarist, bandleader, composer and producer. He was born in 1957 in Mauritius, the son of the poet Edouard Maunick, and moved to the United Kingdom at the age of nine. There he played as one of the original members of Light of the World, a group from the British jazz-funk scene of the late 1970s.

In 1979 he founded Incognito and to this day he is the leader of that band. Incognito is regarded as one of the core names of British acid jazz: a club-oriented sound in which soul, funk and jazz come together. With the group he made fifteen studio albums, besides live albums, remix albums and compilations. As a producer Bluey worked with Paul Weller, George Benson, Maxi Priest and Terry Callier. He also collaborated with Stevie Wonder.

In 2013 his first solo album, Leap of Faith, appeared, on which he combined club-oriented soul-jazz with the calm of an older master. In 2021, together with Gilles Peterson, he formed the group STR4TA, which released the album Aspects on Peterson's label Brownswood Recordings. His importance lies mainly in keeping the jazz-funk sound of the 1970s and 1980s alive, and in the bridge he built between British club culture and American soul and jazz.
artiest/jean-paul-bluey-maunick.listen: Listen to a track by Incognito and notice how the funk guitar, the tight rhythm section and the horns together make a danceable jazz sound.
